title: The Days of Creation
summary: What God made on each day of Creation week (Genesis 1–2).

items.note: "Let there be light"; day and night divided.
Waters above separated from waters below.
Dry land appears; vegetation and fruit trees.
Lights in the heavens for signs, seasons, days and years.
The waters swarm and birds fly across the sky.
"Let us make man in our image"; male and female.
God blesses the seventh day and makes it holy.

title: The Ten Plagues of Egypt
summary: God's judgments on Egypt and its gods before the Exodus (Exodus 7–12).

items.note: The Nile turns to blood; the fish die.
Frogs cover the land.
The magicians: "This is the finger of God."
Swarms of flies, but none in Goshen.
Egypt's livestock die; Israel's are spared.
Boils break out on people and animals.
Thunder, hail and fire, the worst in Egypt's history.
Locusts eat everything the hail left.
Three days of darkness, but light where Israel lived.
At midnight; the Passover lamb's blood protects Israel.

title: The Ten Commandments
summary: The words God spoke from Mount Sinai (Exodus 20; repeated in Deuteronomy 5).

items.note: "You shall have no other gods before me."
No carved image to bow down to or serve.
"You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain."
Six days of work, the seventh a Sabbath to the LORD.
The first commandment with a promise (Eph 6:2).
Do not lie about your neighbor.
Do not desire what belongs to your neighbor.

title: The Judges of Israel
summary: The deliverers God raised up between Joshua and the kings (Judges; 1 Samuel 1–7).

items.note: Caleb's nephew; delivers Israel from Mesopotamia. 40 years of rest.
The left-handed judge who kills Eglon of Moab. 80 years of rest.
Strikes down 600 Philistines with an oxgoad.
Prophetess who judges under her palm tree; Sisera defeated.
Called while threshing wheat; 300 men rout Midian.
Judges Israel 23 years.
Thirty sons on thirty donkeys; judges 22 years.
Defeats Ammon; his rash vow.
Judges 7 years.
Judges 10 years; buried at Aijalon.
Forty sons and thirty grandsons; judges 8 years.
A Nazirite of great strength; judges 20 years against the Philistines.
Priest at Shiloh; judges 40 years.
Prophet and last judge; anoints Saul and David.

title: Kings of the United Kingdom
summary: The three kings who ruled all twelve tribes before the kingdom divided.

items.note: Anointed by Samuel; rejected for disobedience. Reigns from Gibeah.
A man after God's own heart. Seven years at Hebron, then 33 in Jerusalem.
Builds the temple; famous for wisdom, but his heart turns to idols.

note: Solomon began well but turned away late in life (1 Kgs 11:4).

title: Kings of Israel (Northern Kingdom)
summary: The nineteen kings of the ten northern tribes, from the split in 931 BC to Assyria's conquest in 722 BC. Every one is judged to have done evil.

items.note: Sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan.
Killed by Baasha.
Wipes out Jeroboam's house; reigns from Tirzah.
Murdered while drunk.
Reigns seven days; burns the palace over himself.
Buys the hill of Samaria and builds the new capital.
With Jezebel promotes Baal; opposed by Elijah.
Falls through a lattice; inquires of Baal-zebub.
Killed by Jehu.
Destroys Baal worship but keeps the golden calves.
Oppressed by Syria.
Visits the dying Elisha.
Restores Israel's borders; the era of Amos and Hosea.
Reigns six months; the end of Jehu's line.
Reigns one month.
Pays tribute to Assyria.
Assassinated by Pekah.
Assyria takes much of the north.
Last king; Samaria falls to Assyria.

note: Dates follow Edwin Thiele's chronology; several reigns overlap as co-regencies.

title: Kings of Judah (Southern Kingdom)
summary: The rulers of Judah from David's line, from the split in 931 BC to Babylon's destruction of Jerusalem in 586 BC.

items.note: His harsh answer splits the kingdom.
Removes idols and even his grandmother's Asherah.
Sends teachers of the Law; allies with Ahab.
Marries Ahab's daughter Athaliah.
Killed by Jehu.
Seizes the throne and kills the royal heirs, except Joash.
Crowned at seven; repairs the temple.
Defeats Edom, then picks a fight with Israel.
Strong king, struck with leprosy for pride (2 Chr 26:16-21).
Sacrifices his son; appeals to Assyria.
Trusts the LORD; Jerusalem delivered from Sennacherib.
The most wicked king; later repents (2 Chr 33:12-13).
Finds the Book of the Law and leads reform.
Taken to Egypt after three months.
Burns Jeremiah's scroll (Jer 36:23).
Taken to Babylon after three months.
Last king; Jerusalem destroyed.

note: Dates follow Edwin Thiele's chronology; several reigns overlap as co-regencies. Athaliah was not of David's line.

title: The Writing Prophets
summary: The sixteen prophets whose books bear their names: the four major and the twelve minor prophets.

items.note: Prophesies to Judah through four kings; the suffering Servant.
The weeping prophet warns Judah for forty years.
Priest and prophet among the exiles.
Faithful in Babylon's court; visions of the kingdoms.
His marriage pictures God's love for unfaithful Israel.
A locust plague and the day of the LORD; the Spirit poured out.
A shepherd from Tekoa: "Let justice roll down like waters."
Judgment on Edom.
Sent to Nineveh; swallowed by a great fish.
Foretells the ruler from Bethlehem.
The fall of Nineveh.
"The righteous shall live by his faith."
The great day of the LORD.
"Consider your ways": rebuild the temple.
Visions of restoration; the coming King on a donkey.
The last Old Testament prophet; the messenger to come.

title: The Twelve Sons of Jacob
summary: The sons of Jacob (Israel), in birth order, who became the twelve tribes (Genesis 29–35; blessed in Genesis 49).

items.note: Firstborn; loses the birthright (Gen 49:4).
Held hostage in Egypt (Gen 42:24).
Father of the priestly tribe; given no territory.
"The scepter shall not depart from Judah" (Gen 49:10): the line of David and Jesus.
"Dan shall judge his people" (Gen 49:16).
Saves his family in Egypt; his sons Ephraim and Manasseh each become a tribe.
Rachel dies giving birth to him; the tribe of Saul and of Paul.

title: The Feasts of Israel
summary: The LORD's appointed times (Leviticus 23), plus two later feasts. Many point ahead to Christ.

items.note: A weekly day of rest; Christ is our rest (Heb 4:9-10).
Remembers the exodus; "Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed" (1 Cor 5:7).
Seven days without leaven; put away the old leaven (1 Cor 5:8).
The first sheaf offered; Christ the firstfruits of the resurrection (1 Cor 15:20).
Fifty days later; the Spirit poured out (Acts 2:1).
A day of trumpet blasts.
The high priest enters the Most Holy Place (Lev 16; Heb 9:11-12).
Living in booths to remember the wilderness (John 7:2).
Celebrates deliverance in Esther's day.
Remembers the temple rededicated in the silent years.

title: Women of the Bible
summary: Women whose faith, courage and choices shaped the story, from Eve to the early church.

items.note: The mother of all living; the first promise is given to her offspring (3:15).
Abraham's wife; bears Isaac in old age. Buried at Hebron.
Sarah's servant; the God who sees her by the spring on the way to Shur.
Waters Eliezer's camels and becomes Isaac's wife.
Jacob's first wife; mother of Levi and Judah.
Jacob's beloved; mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
Judah's daughter-in-law; in the line of David and of Jesus (Matt 1:3).
Moses' mother; hides him in a basket on the Nile (Exod 2:3).
Moses' wife, daughter of the priest of Midian.
Prophetess; leads the women in song after the Red Sea.
Hides the spies; saved at Jericho; in Jesus' line (Matt 1:5).
Prophetess and judge of Israel.
Kills Sisera with a tent peg.
Betrays Samson to the Philistines.
Widowed in Moab, returns home to Bethlehem.
"Your people shall be my people"; great-grandmother of David.
Prays for a son at Shiloh and gives Samuel to the LORD.
Her wisdom keeps David from bloodshed.
Wife of Uriah, then David; mother of Solomon.
Comes to test Solomon's wisdom.
Ahab's queen; promotes Baal and persecutes the prophets.
Feeds Elijah; her flour and oil never run out.
Builds a room for Elisha; her son is raised.
Prophetess consulted when the Book of the Law is found.
Becomes queen and risks her life to save her people.
Mother of John the Baptist.
"Let it be to me according to your word."
Aged prophetess who speaks of the child Jesus in the temple.
Meets Jesus at Jacob's well and tells her town.
Freed from seven demons; first to see the risen Lord (John 20:16).
Serves Jesus; confesses him as the Christ (John 11:27).
Sits at Jesus' feet; anoints him (John 12:3).
Full of good works; raised by Peter.
Seller of purple; the Lord opens her heart.
With Aquila, a tentmaker and teacher of Apollos (18:26).
Servant of the church at Cenchreae who carries Romans.
Timothy's grandmother and mother, of sincere faith.

title: The Twelve Apostles
summary: The twelve Jesus chose to be with him and to send out (Matthew 10:2-4), plus Matthias and Paul.

items.note: Fisherman; confesses Jesus as the Christ; preaches at Pentecost; writes 1–2 Peter.
Peter's brother; first a disciple of John the Baptist (John 1:40).
A "son of thunder"; first apostle martyred (Acts 12:2).
The disciple Jesus loved; writes the Gospel, three letters and Revelation.
From Bethsaida; brings Nathanael to Jesus.
"An Israelite in whom there is no deceit" (John 1:47); from Cana.
Doubts, then confesses: "My Lord and my God!" (John 20:28).
Tax collector at Capernaum; writes the first Gospel.
Sometimes called James the Less.
Asks Jesus a question at the Last Supper (John 14:22).
Once a member (or in the spirit) of the Zealots.
Betrays Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
Chosen by lot to replace Judas.
Apostle to the Gentiles, called by the risen Christ.

title: Miracles of Jesus
summary: Signs Jesus performed, in an approximate harmony of the Gospels (John 20:30-31).

items.note: His first sign, at a wedding.
Healed from a distance.
Peter, James and John leave all to follow him.

items.t: Demon cast out in the synagogue
items.note: "Be silent, and come out of him!"
She gets up and serves them.
"I will; be clean."
"Your sins are forgiven."

items.t: Man healed at the pool of Bethesda
items.note: Lame 38 years: "Get up, take up your bed."
On the Sabbath, in the synagogue.
"Not even in Israel have I found such faith."
Stops the funeral procession.
"Peace! Be still!"
The man is found clothed and in his right mind.

items.t: Woman with the issue of blood
items.note: Healed by touching his garment.
"Talitha cumi": "Little girl, arise."
"According to your faith be it done to you."
The crowds marvel.
Five loaves and two fish; twelve baskets left over.
Peter walks too, then sinks.
"Even the dogs eat the children's crumbs."
"Ephphatha": "Be opened."
Seven loaves; seven baskets left over.
He sees everything clearly.
"I believe; help my unbelief!"
Pays the temple tax.
"Go, wash in the pool of Siloam."

items.t: Crippled woman healed on the Sabbath
items.note: Bent over eighteen years.
At a Pharisee's house on the Sabbath.
"Lazarus, come out."
Only the Samaritan returns to give thanks.
"Your faith has made you well."
"Have faith in God."
At his arrest.
After the resurrection: 153 fish.

title: Parables of Jesus
summary: Stories Jesus told to teach about the kingdom of God (Matthew 13:34-35).

items.note: House on the rock, house on the sand.
New wine needs new wineskins.
The one forgiven more loves more.
The seed is the word of God (Luke 8:11).
Separated at the harvest.
The smallest seed becomes a tree.
A little leaven leavens the whole lump.
Sells all he has to buy the field.
Good and bad fish sorted at the end.
Forgiven much, he refuses to forgive little.
"Who is my neighbor?"
Persistence in prayer.
"This night your soul is required of you."
Ready for the master's return.
One more year to bear fruit.
The invited make excuses.
The tower builder and the king at war.
Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
"This my son was dead, and is alive again."
"You cannot serve God and money."
A great chasm fixed.
"We have only done our duty."
Always pray and do not lose heart.
"God, be merciful to me, a sinner!"
The last will be first.
Faithful with a little.
Who did the father's will?
The stone the builders rejected.
Many are called, few are chosen.
Know the signs of the times.
Keep your lamps ready.
"Well done, good and faithful servant."
"As you did it to one of the least of these…"

note: Rich man and Lazarus, and the sheep and goats, are not called parables in the text; many lists include them.

title: The "I Am" Statements of Jesus
summary: Jesus' sayings in John's Gospel that echo God's name, "I AM" (Exodus 3:14).

items.note: After feeding the five thousand.

items.t: "I am the light of the world"
items.note: Repeated before healing the man born blind (9:5).
They pick up stones to throw at him.

items.t: "I am the door of the sheep"
items.note: "If anyone enters by me, he will be saved."
He lays down his life for the sheep.

items.t: "I am the resurrection and the life"
items.note: To Martha, before raising Lazarus.

items.t: "I am the way, and the truth, and the life"
items.note: "No one comes to the Father except through me."
"Apart from me you can do nothing."

title: The Beatitudes
summary: The blessings that open the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5:3-10).

items.note: …for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
…for they shall be comforted.
…for they shall inherit the earth.

items.t: Those who hunger and thirst for righteousness
items.note: …for they shall be satisfied.
…for they shall receive mercy.
…for they shall see God.
…for they shall be called sons of God.
…for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

title: The Seven Sayings from the Cross
summary: Jesus' last words as he was crucified, in their likely order.

items.t: "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do."
"Today you will be with me in Paradise."
items.note: To the repentant thief.
Entrusts Mary to John.

items.t: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"
items.note: Quoting Psalm 22:1.
To fulfill the Scripture.

items.t: "Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!"
items.note: Quoting Psalm 31:5.

title: Conversions in Acts
summary: How people became Christians in the book of Acts: what they heard, believed and did.

items.note: Heard Peter preach; cut to the heart; repented and were baptized (2:37-38).
Believed Philip's preaching and were baptized, men and women.
Believed and was baptized.
Heard Jesus preached from Isaiah 53; baptized on the road.
Saw the Lord; prayed three days; baptized to wash away his sins (22:16).
The first Gentiles; the Spirit falls, then they are baptized.
The Lord opened her heart; baptized.
"What must I do to be saved?" Baptized the same hour of the night.
Hearing, believed and were baptized.
Knew only John's baptism; baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

title: Baptisms in the New Testament
summary: Every baptism the New Testament records, from John at the Jordan to Paul at Ephesus, with what led to each.
note: For the teaching on baptism, see Romans 6:3-4, Galatians 3:27, Colossians 2:12 and 1 Peter 3:21.

items.note: John baptizes in the Jordan those confessing their sins: a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins (Mark 1:4-5).
Baptized by John "to fulfill all righteousness"; the Spirit descends like a dove and the Father speaks (3:15-17).
Jesus' disciples baptize more people than John, though Jesus himself does not baptize (4:1-2).
John baptizes there "because water was plentiful there."
Jesus sends the apostles to make disciples of all nations, baptizing them; "whoever believes and is baptized will be saved" (Mark 16:16).
"Repent and be baptized … for the forgiveness of your sins" (2:38).
Believed Philip's preaching of the kingdom and the name of Jesus.
Believed and was baptized, then stayed close to Philip.
Both went down into the water, and Philip baptized him; he went on his way rejoicing.
"Rise and be baptized and wash away your sins" (22:16).
The first Gentiles; Peter commands them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.
The Lord opened her heart to listen to Paul, by the river outside the city.

items.t: The Philippian jailer and his household
items.note: "What must I do to be saved?" Baptized the same hour of the night.
Hearing Paul, they believed and were baptized. Paul himself baptized Crispus, Gaius and Stephanas' household (1 Cor 1:14-16).
They knew only John's baptism; they are baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

title: The Hall of Faith (Hebrews 11)
summary: "Without faith it is impossible to please him": the faithful the writer of Hebrews remembers.

items.note: Offered a better sacrifice than Cain (Gen 4:4).
Taken up so that he did not see death (Gen 5:24).
Built the ark in reverent fear (Gen 6:22).
Went out, not knowing where he was going (Gen 12:4).
Received power to conceive (Gen 21:2).
Blessed Jacob and Esau (Gen 27).
Blessed Joseph's sons (Gen 48).
Gave directions about his bones (Gen 50:25).
Hid him three months, not afraid of the king's edict (Exod 2:2).
Chose mistreatment with God's people over Egypt's treasures.
Crossed as on dry land (Exod 14:22).
Fell after being encircled seven days (Josh 6:20).
Welcomed the spies in peace (Josh 2).

items.t: Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the prophets
items.note: "Time would fail me to tell…"

title: The Seven Churches of Revelation
summary: Jesus' letters to seven churches in the province of Asia (Revelation 2–3), in the order a messenger would travel.

items.note: Hard-working and sound, but has abandoned its first love.
"Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life."
Where Satan's throne is; tolerates the teaching of Balaam.
Growing in love and service, but tolerates "Jezebel."
"You have the reputation of being alive, but you are dead."
Little power but faithful: "I have set before you an open door."
Lukewarm: "I stand at the door and knock."

title: Paul's Letters
summary: Paul's thirteen letters in the order they were likely written, and where he wrote them. Dates are approximate; some are debated.

items.note: Saved by grace through faith, not by the works of the Law.
Encouragement for a young church; the Lord's return.
The day of the Lord has not yet come; keep working.
Division, morality, worship, love (ch. 13) and the resurrection (ch. 15).
Paul defends his ministry; strength in weakness.
The gospel, the power of God for salvation.
The church as Christ's body; the armor of God.
The supremacy of Christ.
Receive Onesimus back as a brother.
Joy in Christ: "To live is Christ, and to die is gain."
Order and leadership in the church.
Appoint elders; teach sound doctrine.
His last letter: "I have fought the good fight."

title: The Fruit of the Spirit
summary: The fruit the Spirit produces in a Christian's life (Galatians 5:22-23).

items.note: "Love is patient and kind" (1 Cor 13:4).
"Rejoice in the Lord always" (Phil 4:4).
The peace of God that surpasses understanding (Phil 4:7).
Bearing with one another in love (Eph 4:2).
"Be kind to one another" (Eph 4:32).
"Let us not grow weary of doing good" (Gal 6:9).
"Be faithful unto death" (Rev 2:10).
Restore others in a spirit of gentleness (Gal 6:1).
"Against such things there is no law."

title: The Armor of God
summary: "Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand" (Ephesians 6:10-18).

items.note: Readiness to go with the good news.
Extinguishes the flaming darts of the evil one.
The word of God (Heb 4:12).
"Praying at all times in the Spirit."

summary: The miracles John records "so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God" (John 20:31).

Healed by a word, from twenty miles away.
Lame for 38 years.
